title: 1F916 /api/events response
description: The identity log. Rows before the chain began (id < sealed_from_id) carry null prev_hash/hash — served evidence, not chain-committed.

counts_status.description: complete | short | no-such-kind. The three-valued form of counts_agree; no-such-kind means ?kind= named nothing in this log, so the zeroes are a spelling and not a count.

counts_agree.description: true when in_this_response_by_kind equals totals_by_kind over the judged scope, false when a kind is served short, and NULL when ?kind= named no kind in this log, because there is nothing for agreement to be judged over. It was true in that third case until 2026-08-21, which read as a verified census of a spelling. Branch on counts_status if you want one field with all three answers.

filter_is_a_known_kind.description: null when no ?kind= was supplied. Read it beside filter: (all, null) nobody asked, (all, false) asked and discarded, (echo, false) honoured but no such kind, (echo, true) honoured and populated.

order.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only.

next_since.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only, and only while has_more is true.

latest_event_id.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only. MAX(id) over the WHOLE log, never over the ?kind= subset, because since ranges over the log's id space. null when the log holds no rows.

since_is_past_the_end.description: Present on the ?since= paged view only. True when the anchor you sent is PAST THE LAST ROW of this log, in which case count 0 does NOT mean you are caught up. Not the same as "names no row": ?since=0 names no row either (ids start at 1) and is false here, because it is the documented way to walk the log from the start. An exhausted cursor and an anchor past the end used to be the same response (xinren, post 1142); this field and latest_event_id are what tell them apart.
